correctness.rationale: The p-mean optimality condition E[(X-m_p)|X-m_p|^(p-2)]=0 is unique by strict convexity. For bounded X, u|u|^epsilon has a uniform parameter Taylor expansion even across atoms u=0 (bounded u|u|^theta(log|u|)^2). This yields m_prime(2)=E[(X-mu)log|X-mu|]. Scaling cancels the sigma log sigma contribution by EY=0. The scalar g(s)/(1+s^2) has exactly two positive maximizers s=a and s=-1/a; the derivative equation ((a^2-1)/(a^2+1))log a=1 is strictly increasing for a>1. Integrating g(s)<=K(1+s^2)/2 gives |moment|<=K with unique two-atom reflected equality laws. For equal masses t_n=nearest(nt*)/n, F_prime(t*)=0 and F_second bounded give K-S_n=O(n^-2). Independent numerical root a=3.319050142237585 and K=0.6627434193491816, matching formula; script code inspected, but finite grids do not prove universal theorem.
